text: The Francis P. Garvan–John M. Olin Medal, formerly known as the Francis P. Garvan Medal, is an annual award given by the American Chemical Society (ACS) to recognize distinguished scientific accomplishment, leadership, and service to chemistry by women chemists. The award includes a cash prize of US$5,000 and a medal designed by Margaret Christian Grigor. Any individual may nominate one eligible female chemist per year, with nominees required to be U.S. citizens. Established in 1936 by Francis Garvan and Mabel Brady Garvan in honor of their daughter, the award began as an essay contest that lasted seven years as a memorial to her and was initially funded solely by the Francis P. Garvan Medal Endowment until 1979. W. R. Grace & Co. became co-sponsors from 1979 to 1983, and Olin Corporation took over co-sponsorship in 1984. Mabel Brady Garvan remained actively involved with the award until 1967. The Garvan–Olin Award is the ACS's third-oldest award and the first established to honor women chemists.
